Theme

Kitchen, meals & drinks

recline at table verb

also take your place at table, sit down to dinner, lie down to eat, take a seat at table

classical

Plaut. Most. 308: Age accumbe igitur.
Cic. Mur. 74: cotīdiānīs epulīs in rōbore (Lewis & Short)

accumbō, accumbere, accubuī, accubitum

verb, third conjugation

lie down at table, take one’s place on the dining couch

The Romans ate lying on couches, propped on the left elbow; accumbe is what a host says where we say “sit down”. In summō accumbere, to take the top place.

Other words

  • accubō, accubāre — be lying at table (the state, where accumbō is the act)

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Plaut. Bacch. 81b: ut lepidus cum lepidā accubet; Cic. Cat. 2.10: accubantēs in convīviīs (Lewis & Short)

  • discumbō, discumbere, discubuī, discubitum — take one’s places at table (of the whole company)

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 5.1.4: discubuimus omnēs praeter illam (Lewis & Short); Verg. A. 1.708 (Lewis & Short)

    Especially frequent from the Augustan age on (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • Age accumbe igitur. Cedo aquam manibus, puere, appōne hīc mēnsulam.

    Come on then, take your place. Boy, bring water for our hands, put the little table here.Plaut. Most. 308

  • Tū Sagaristiō, accumbe in summō.

    You, Sagaristio, take the top place.Plaut. Pers. 767

See also dinner, guest, dining room, sit down!, table.
